artists.biography:
The Rolling Stones are an English rock band formed in London in 1962. The first settled line-up consisted of Brian Jones on guitar and harmonica, Ian Stewart on piano, Mick Jagger on lead vocals and harmonica, Keith Richards on guitar and backing vocals, Bill Wyman on bass and Charlie Watts on drums. Jones founded and led the band, but Jagger and Richards assumed leadership after becoming the primary songwriters. Jones' increasing physical and mental troubles forced his departure from the band two weeks prior to his drowning death in 1969. Since Wyman retired in 1993, full band members have been Jagger, Richards, Watts and guitarist Ronnie Wood who joined in 1975, replacing Mick Taylor (who had followed Jones). The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducted the Rolling Stones in 1989. Rolling Stone magazine ranked them fourth on the "100 Greatest Artists of All Time" list and their album sales are estimated at more than 200 million worldwide.

The Rolling Stones were in the vanguard of the "British Invasion" of English bands that became popular in the U.S. in the mid-sixties. They have released twenty-four studio albums, eleven live albums and numerous compilations. Their album Sticky Fingers (1971) began a string of eight consecutive studio albums reaching number one in the United States. Their most recent album of new material, A Bigger Bang, was released in 2005. In 2008, Billboard magazine ranked the Rolling Stones at number ten on "The Billboard Top All-Time Artists" and as the second most successful group in the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

The Rolling Stones' advent brought greater international recognition to the primitive urban blues typified by Chess Records' artist Muddy Waters, writer of "Rollin' Stone", the song for which the band is named. Critic and musicologist Robert Palmer said their endurance and relevance stems from being "rooted in traditional verities, in rhythm-and-blues and soul music" while "more ephemeral pop fashions have come and gone". In 2012 the band celebrated their 50th anniversary.

lastfm.wiki_content: "Out of Our Heads" is the third studio album by the English rock band the Rolling Stones, released in two editions with different covers and track listings. In the United States, London Records issued it on 30 July 1965 as the band's fourth American album, while Decca Records released the UK edition on 24 September 1965 as the third British album. The album features the band members Mick Jagger, Brian Jones, Keith Richards, Bill Wyman, and Charlie Watts, with additional contributions from former member Ian Stewart. It was produced by the group's manager Andrew Loog Oldham. Similar to the band's previous albums, "Out of Our Heads" primarily contains covers of American blues, soul, and rhythm and blues songs, alongside original material written by the group (four of 12 tracks on the UK version and six of 12 on the US version). The American edition includes "(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction," which became the band's first number-one hit in the United States and also topped charts in several other countries, including the UK. "Out of Our Heads" reached number one on the US Billboard 200 album chart and peaked at number two in the UK. The US edition largely features mid-1960s soul covers and original tracks such as "The Last Time," "Play with Fire," and "Satisfaction," which draw on the band's R&B and blues influences while adopting a more guitar-based contemporary style. Soul covers on the album include Marvin Gaye's "Hitch Hike," Solomon Burke's "Cry to Me," and Sam Cooke's "Good Times." The UK edition is described as a mixture of rock and roll and rhythm and blues. The album opens with a cover of "She Said Yeah," characterised as a proto-punk track, while the remaining songs form a foundation for what would later be described as blue-eyed soul, including "That's How Strong My Love Is," noted for its deep soul style. perplexity.description:
Out of Our Heads is a pivotal 1965 Rolling Stones album that captures the band in transition, moving from their early reliance on American blues and R&B covers toward a more confident songwriting identity. Released in a UK edition on Decca, it blends raw rock energy with earthy blues phrasing and a sharper, more self-assured attack, with standout material including “(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction,” one of the defining singles of the decade.

The album’s sound is looser and more swaggering than the Stones’ earliest records, but also more focused in its sense of purpose. Its mix of cover versions and original songs shows the group still rooted in Chicago blues and soul, yet already shaping the harder-edged rock persona that would make them one of the era’s most important bands. The record was a major commercial breakthrough and is widely seen as a crucial step in the Stones’ evolution from promising British R&B upstarts into world-class rock auteurs.
